title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
authors: Hang Du, Brice Huang, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman
abstract: We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $β< 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.
summary: This work provides a rigorous mathematical proof demonstrating that simulated annealing efficiently samples the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model up to criticality. It achieves this by establishing key mixing properties, such as the weak Poincaré inequality, and by developing advanced techniques to bound the covariance and derivatives of model observables.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model, particularly near the critical inverse temperature $ eta < 1$. It also focuses on bounding derivatives of key observables related to the model's structure.
main_result: They prove that simulated annealing can sample the SK model to arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy ($	ext{dTV} \le N^{-a}$) in $O(a,  eta(N \log N))$ steps, and establish crucial bounds on the covariance matrix and derivatives of magnetization-related functions.
method: The analysis combines techniques from stochastic localization, weak Poincaré inequalities, and rigorous moment estimates derived through repeated differentiation of model identities.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model, an Ising spin glass with random interactions. The analysis often utilizes a 'planted model' approximation to make the stochastic localization trajectory tractable.
key_observables: Total Variation Distance ($	ext{dTV}$), Weak Poincaré Inequality, Covariance Matrix ($	ext{Cov}(\mu_{ eta W})$), Magnetization ($m(B)$), and correlation functions ($\kappa(B)$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature $ eta < 1$, system size $N$, and the accuracy parameter $a$ (for $	ext{dTV} \le N^{-a}$).
main_assumptions: The proof relies on establishing the weak Poincaré inequality and bounding the covariance matrix, often requiring approximations like the planted model and assuming the validity of prior moment estimates.
paper_structure: The paper develops results sequentially: first proving the weak Poincaré inequality (Theorem 1.2) for the SK model, then establishing covariance bounds (Theorem 1.3) via stochastic localization, and finally using advanced differentiation techniques (Lemmas A.7-A.13) to bound higher-order derivatives of observables.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical tools developed for bounding mixing times and analyzing high-dimensional random energy landscapes (like the SK model) are foundational for understanding complex energy minimization problems in quantum many-body physics and optimization.
